name: Estonia
tagline: A narrow menu — but two free engineering degrees on it
summary: Estonia has a reputation for teaching in English, and at master's level that is true. At bachelor's level it is not. The official national listing contains only about 28 to 30 English-taught bachelor's degrees in the entire country, so your menu is short and you should treat it as a list to read end to end rather than a system to search. The one genuinely striking offer is at TalTech, where Cyber Security Engineering and Integrated Engineering are free for EU and EEA citizens — as a Danish student you would pay nothing for either.
whyConsider: TalTech's Cyber Security Engineering and Integrated Engineering are free for EU/EEA citizens. Non-EU students pay 7,000 and 6,000 euros a year for the same degrees.

Where you do pay, it is cheap by European standards: Tartu's Business Administration is 4,200 euros a year, Tallinn University's Liberal Arts in Humanities 4,200, and the Academy of Music and Theatre charges EU students 1,750.
Living costs are among the lowest in the EU — dormitories from 150 to 350 euros a month, and public transport in Tallinn is free once you register your residence.
You need no work permit and there is no cap on your hours, as long as you keep passing a full course load.
Tallinn University's Baltic Film, Media and Arts School describes itself as the only place in northern Europe teaching film, television and audiovisual production in English.
watchOuts: Only around 28 to 30 English-taught bachelor's degrees exist nationally. Estonia's English-taught provision is overwhelmingly postgraduate — plan on reading the whole list rather than filtering a big catalogue.

The Estonian Academy of Arts has no English-taught bachelor's degree at all. Every one of its bachelor's programmes is taught in Estonian and needs B2 Estonian to apply. Its ten English programmes are master's and doctoral only.
Most English-taught bachelor's degrees charge tuition to EU citizens too. The TalTech engineering exception is the exception, not the rule.

Enrolling at a university does not give you Estonian health insurance. International students are not covered by the health insurance fund unless they are employed or hold permanent residence — bring your Danish EHIC and consider supplementary cover.

Almost nothing about the University of Tartu's and TalTech's own admissions is verifiable from outside: their websites block automated access, so their deadlines, application fees, entrance tests and any minimum IB points are unknown. Email them directly.
The official living-cost figures are from a 2019 survey and are almost certainly understated today.

notes: The full IB Diploma certifies completion of secondary education and gives access to Estonian higher education without a separate nostrification step.

Only the full Diploma appears to count — DP Course Results are reported not to be sufficient. This rule comes from summaries of the Estonian ENIC/NARIC material rather than from a page that could actually be loaded, so confirm it with Harno before relying on it.
No Estonian institution publishes a minimum IB point score, and no IB-to-Estonian grade conversion table could be found. The Harno pages that would hold it block automated access.
Whether Estonian universities make conditional offers on predicted IB grades is unknown. Nobody publishes an answer either way, so ask directly.

Tallinn University is the one institution with fully readable selection rules: you need completed secondary education at at least 60 percent of the maximum possible result, you sit an admission exam that may have several parts and runs several times during the application window, and the enrolment threshold is 65 points out of 100.

portal.name: DreamApply Estonia — one interface shared by nine institutions, but each sets its own deadlines and decisions

deadlines.label: Tallinn University, all bachelor's programmes, autumn 2027 intake
deadlines.notes: The only confirmed 2027-entry deadline anywhere in Estonia. Treat it as your anchor date and assume other universities will land in a similar window until they publish.

deadlines.label: Other institutions, bachelor's
deadlines.notes: Not published as of September 2026. For 2026 entry, Study in Estonia described bachelor's deadlines as typically April to May, and DreamApply's own overview says typically around 1 June. Check each university individually from late 2026.

deadlines.label: Tallinn University dormitory offers
deadlines.notes: Published as "June", with no day given. You get a link to the housing application form after official acceptance. For 2026/27 the first access day was 22 August.

steps: Read the national list of English-taught bachelor's degrees at studyinestonia.ee end to end. There are only about thirty, and that is faster than searching.
Decide early whether the free TalTech engineering route is for you, because it changes the cost of the whole plan.
Create one DreamApply account at estonia.dreamapply.com — nine institutions share it, including Tartu, TalTech and Tallinn University.
Check each university's own deadline separately. They are not aligned. Tallinn University closes 1 March 2027; the others had not published 2027 dates when this was researched.

Submit your secondary school certificate, transcript, proof of English, passport ID page and any programme-specific documents. If you hold an IB Diploma, Tallinn University accepts your graduation documents as English proof with no test.
Pay the application fee where one applies — 100 euros at Tallinn University, covering up to two programmes. Other institutions' fees are not published.
Sit the admission exam if your programme has one. Tallinn University runs its exam several times during the application period.

Once admitted, apply for a dormitory place, then register your residence with the local government within three months of arriving and apply for an Estonian ID card within one month of getting your right of residence.
application.selectionNotes: Admission is decentralised — you apply to the institution, not to a central body, even though nine of them share the DreamApply interface. Tallinn University is the only institution whose selection mechanics are fully published: a 60 percent secondary school result to be eligible, an admission exam, and a 65-out-of-100 enrolment threshold. The University of Tartu and TalTech both block automated access to their sites, so what they use for selection is unknown from the outside.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Approximately 28 to 30 nationally. Two reads of the official listing gave 28 and 29 entries, and DreamApply's own filter showed 30. Study in Estonia's quotable national figure is 'more than 150 degree programmes fully taught in English', but that counts every level and is dominated by master's degrees. Tallinn University has the widest bachelor's choice with six.
language.englishProof: Tallinn University states it most clearly: students who have completed International Baccalaureate studies can submit their graduation documents as proof of English proficiency, so no IELTS is needed. It also exempts anyone who completed previous education fully in English in an EU or EEA country, which covers a Danish IB school. If a test is required, it asks for IELTS Academic 6.0 with at least 5.5 in each component, Cambridge B2 First, C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency at 169 overall, or PTE Academic 59. Estonian Business School asks for English at at least B2.
notes: Estonian-language programmes at public universities are generally free through state-funded places, but they are not a realistic route for a Danish school leaver.
The Estonian Academy of Arts requires B2 Estonian for every bachelor's programme it runs.
Tallinn University's TOEFL minimum could not be read reliably — the figure extracted from its page was corrupt. Check it directly if you need the TOEFL route.
Test results must generally be no more than two years old at the start of studies; Cambridge certificates are valid for ten.

tuitionEuEea.value: Varies sharply by programme. Free for EU/EEA citizens on TalTech's Cyber Security Engineering and Integrated Engineering. Otherwise: University of Tartu Business Administration 4,200 euros a year, Science and Technology 6,000, Medicine 13,200; TalTech International Business Administration and Law 5,000 each; Tallinn University 4,200 to 5,400 depending on programme; Estonian Business School 7,730 to 8,100; Estonian Academy of Music and Theatre 1,750; Estonian University of Life Sciences Veterinary Medicine 9,800; Baltic Methodist Theological Seminary 2,600. Nationally, Study in Estonia quotes a range of 1,500 to 15,000 euros.
tuitionEuEea.year: 2026/27 — 2027/28 fees were not published as of September 2026

tuitionNonEu.value: Higher where a distinction is made: TalTech Cyber Security Engineering 7,000 euros a year and Integrated Engineering 6,000 where EU students pay nothing; Estonian Academy of Music and Theatre 7,700 against 1,750 for EU students; Estonian Entrepreneurship UAS 7,520 against 7,120. Most other programmes charge the same to everyone.

costs.applicationFee: 100 euros at Tallinn University, non-refundable, covering up to two programmes. A Danish student pays it — the waivers are for people educated in Estonia, Estonian citizens, long-term residence holders and, for the 2026/27 intake, Ukrainian citizens. No other institution's fee could be verified.

livingCostMonthly.value: Study in Estonia says around 300 to 500 euros a month, with dormitories at 150 to 350 and private flats at 350 to 750. Food comes to roughly 300 a month for comfortable living, and a university cafeteria lunch costs 5 to 8 euros.
livingCostMonthly.year: 2019 survey data, published on a current page

notes: The survey behind the 300-to-500-euro figure is 2019 iGraduate data and is seven years old. Budget above it.
Public transport in Tallinn is free for registered residents, including international students. Registering your residence is what unlocks it.
In Tartu a monthly student transport ticket is 7.67 euros and a single student ticket 51 cents. The intercity bus from Tallinn to Tartu costs 8 to 12 euros.
Doctoral studies in Estonia are free of tuition regardless of nationality.

funding: Danish SU for a full degree abroad, at DKK 7,426 a month before tax for students living away from home in 2026. Estonia is not a Nordic country for SU purposes, so support is capped at four years rather than programme length plus twelve months.

The biggest saving available to you is not a scholarship at all — it is the zero tuition on TalTech's Cyber Security Engineering and Integrated Engineering for EU/EEA citizens. Do check with TalTech whether that free status carries conditions on academic progress.

The Estonian National Scholarship pays 350 euros a month, but at bachelor's level it can only be applied for in fields related to Estonian language and culture, and eligibility is limited to a list of countries whose contents could not be checked. Denmark's inclusion is unconfirmed.
Compatriots Scholarships are for young expatriate Estonians on Estonian-language curricula, so they do not apply.

University tuition waivers are the realistic route where you do pay. Tallinn University publishes a table: 50 to 100 percent for Baltic Film, Media and Arts from the second semester, 100 percent for two Governance, Law and Society awards, and 50 percent awards in several humanities programmes, all merit-based. Euro amounts and most deadlines are not published.

The University of Tartu reportedly offers tuition reductions of 25, 50 or 100 percent granted a semester at a time, and from 2026/27 no longer offers waivers to newly admitted students from outside the EU/EEA — which structurally improves an EU applicant's odds. This comes from summary text only, because Tartu's site could not be loaded.

Estonian performance stipends, the need-based study allowance and the Estonian student loan could not be checked at all — whether a Danish citizen in an English-taught programme qualifies for any of them is unknown. Do not count on them.
Ignore anything you read about Dora Plus. Sources conflict about whether it still exists, and it was in any case a master's and doctoral mobility instrument, not a bachelor's tuition scholarship.
workRights: You need no separate work permit and there is no limit on your hours. The one condition is academic: you must pass a full course load, roughly 30 ECTS a semester, and finish within the nominal duration. The minimum wage was 820 euros gross a month in 2024 and the average full-time salary 1,832 euros gross in 2023 — both figures are dated.
residency: As an EU citizen you register your place of residence with the local government of wherever you live, within three months of entering Estonia. You then apply for an Estonian ID card within one month of obtaining the temporary right of residence. The ID card fee, its validity period and the personal identification code process could not be verified — the police and border guard website blocks automated access. Registering is worth doing promptly for a practical reason: in Tallinn it makes public transport free.
housing: Tallinn University's dormitory at Karu 17 is on the main city-centre campus, double rooms only, at 215 to 230 euros a month for a 14 square metre room and 245 to 260 for a 17 square metre one. Rent includes communal costs, wireless internet, bed linen and laundry, and the deposit runs from 470 to 550 euros. Offers go out in June after acceptance. In Tartu, Tartu Student Village runs eight residences through campus.ee, but its prices are not published. Nationally, Study in Estonia puts the average dormitory cost including utilities at around 350 euros a month. Private rentals go through kv.ee and city24.ee.
healthcare: This is the one thing students get wrong. Enrolling at an Estonian university does not give you Estonian health insurance — international students are not covered by the Health Insurance Fund unless they are employed or hold permanent or long-term residence. Bring your Danish EHIC, the blue card, and understand that it covers public treatment at Estonian rates with the same patient co-payments Estonians pay, and nothing private. Supplementary cover is sensible. Emergency services on 112 are free and available around the clock, and specialists including psychiatrists, dentists and ophthalmologists can be seen without a referral. Taking a part-time job is one way into the state system.

institutions.name: University of Tartu
institutions.englishBachelors: 3 — Business Administration (4,200 euros a year), Science and Technology (6,000), and a six-year integrated Medicine (13,200)
institutions.note: Estonia's flagship and one of the oldest universities in northern Europe, with around 15,500 students. Its own website blocks automated access, so its deadlines, application fee, entrance tests, English minimums and any IB requirements could not be verified — email admissions@ut.ee before you plan around it.

institutions.name: Tallinn University of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: 4 — Cyber Security Engineering and Integrated Engineering, both free for EU/EEA citizens, plus International Business Administration and Law at 5,000 euros a year
institutions.note: The only technical university in Estonia, with around 11,000 students, and the single best-value option in the country for a Danish student: two English-taught engineering degrees that cost EU citizens nothing while non-EU students pay 6,000 to 7,000 euros. Its website also blocks automated access, so deadlines, entrance tests and the exact conditions attached to the free places are unverified.

institutions.name: Tallinn University
institutions.englishBachelors: 6 — Liberal Arts in Humanities (4,200 euros), Crossmedia (4,600), Liberal Arts in Social Sciences (4,600), Audiovisual Media (4,800), Politics and Governance (4,800), Law (5,400)
institutions.note: The widest choice of English-taught bachelor's degrees in Estonia, and by far the most transparent institution in the country — it is the only one that publishes firm 2027 dates (1 November 2026 to 1 March 2027), its selection thresholds, and a clear statement that IB graduation documents count as proof of English. Its Baltic Film, Media and Arts School calls itself the only institution in northern Europe teaching film and television in English.

institutions.name: Estonian Business School
institutions.englishBachelors: 3 — Impactful Entrepreneurship (7,730 euros a year), International Business Administration (7,730), Product and Technology Management (8,100)
institutions.note: A private, non-profit business university of around 1,400 students, and the first institution in the Soviet Union to teach business in English. It is the most expensive option on this list and makes no EU versus non-EU distinction. Its deadlines, application fee, entrance procedure and position on the IB are all unpublished — it states only that it wants secondary education and English at B2.

institutions.name: Estonian Academy of Arts
institutions.englishBachelors: None. Every bachelor's programme is taught in Estonian and needs at least B2 Estonian to apply. Its ten English-taught international programmes are master's and doctoral.
institutions.note: Estonia's only public university for art, design and architecture, with around 1,200 students — and completely closed to you at bachelor's level unless you reach B2 Estonian first. Worth knowing about as a master's destination instead.

institutions.name: Estonian University of Life Sciences
institutions.note: Around 2,900 students and a top-100 world position in agriculture and forestry. Its English-taught veterinary degree is one of relatively few in Europe and worth knowing about if that is your plan, though at 9,800 euros a year it is not cheap.

institutions.name: Estonian Academy of Music and Theatre
institutions.englishBachelors: 2 — Classical Music Performance and Composition and Improvisational Music, both 1,750 euros a year for EU students and 7,700 for non-EU
institutions.note: The cheapest English-taught bachelor's degrees in Estonia for an EU citizen, and one of the largest EU-versus-non-EU price gaps anywhere on this list. Audition requirements were not researched.

institutions.name: Estonian Aviation Academy
institutions.englishBachelors: 2 listed — Commercial Air Transport Pilot (8,100 euros a year) and Commercial Aviation Management (3,780), but the management programme had no intake in 2026/27
institutions.note: A small specialist academy next to Tartu Airport, covering piloting, air traffic services and aircraft engineering. Check whether the aviation management degree is running before you plan on it — it was suspended for 2026/27. Checked 2026-09-23: the academy has moved from eava.ee to lennuakadeemia.ee, its Estonian name; the old domain still redirects but should not be relied on.

institutions.name: Tartu Applied Health Sciences University
institutions.note: Renamed from Tartu Health Care College at the start of 2025, so search under the new name. It is the only place in Estonia training radiology technicians and bioanalysts. Whether it teaches anything in English at bachelor's level could not be confirmed.

institutions.name: Tallinn Health University of Applied Sciences
institutions.note: Appears on the national list with one English-taught bachelor's degree, Assistant Pharmacist. Its founding year and official website could not be verified, so treat everything beyond that programme entry as unchecked.

institutions.name: Estonian Entrepreneurship University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: 3 — Creativity and Business Innovation, Game Design and Development, Software Development and Entrepreneurship, at 7,120 euros a year for EU students and 7,520 for non-EU
institutions.note: Worth a look if game design or software entrepreneurship is your thing, since those are hard to find in English in the Baltics. Its city, founding year and website could not be verified from any source that loaded.

institutions.name: Baltic Methodist Theological Seminary
institutions.englishBachelors: 1 — Theology and Mission, 2,600 euros a year
institutions.note: The cheapest English-taught bachelor's degree on the national list after the music academy. A very small, specialised seminary — its city, founding year and admissions process could not be verified.
